conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: REWRITE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: "Transfer of control following the successful or unsuccessful execution of the REWRITE operation depends on the presence or absence of the optional INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY phrases ... (See 9.1.14, Invalid key condition.)" KeyedIoEmitter.EmitRewrite captures the status, stores FILE STATUS, calls EmitUseHook(invalidKeyHandled: INVALID phrase present) and EmitInvalid(status, phrase) - INVALID arm on the invalid-key class, NOT INVALID arm on success. Probe pd.cob: absent slot -> 'IK7 ST=23' (INVALID arm only), success -> 'NIK1 ST=00' (NOT arm only), 44 -> neither arm (9.1.14: not an invalid key and not successful). Sequential-organization phrases are screened by SR2 (part 2's row). KeyedIoDifferentialTests.Keyed_NotInvalidKey_RunsOnlyOnSuccess is a legacy-differential (AssertSameAsLegacy) and does not qualify, so test-ref empty. cite.py --check 14.9.35.4 GR19 / 9.1.14 -> OK. [editions as adjudicated: 2023; ISO 1989:2023 Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change to this rule (E.3.3 item 41 touches GR10 only), so 2014 identically; the 1985/2002 wording is not derivable from the 2023 text]
rows.rule-text: Transfer of control following the successful or unsuccessful execution of the REWRITE operation depends on the presence or absence of the optional INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY phrases in the REWRITE statement. (See 9.1.14, Invalid key condition.)

rows.subject: REWRITE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: "The number of bytes ... after any changes made to the record length by the FORMAT clause shall not be larger than the largest or smaller than the smallest number of bytes allowed by the RECORD IS VARYING clause ... If this rule is violated ... '44'." The emitters pass the DEPENDING item's content as the length (13.18.43.4 GR13 a)) or -1 (image length); SequentialConnector.Rewrite and Stored (relative/indexed) return RecordSizeViolation '44' outside [VaryMin, VaryMax]. Probe pd.cob: LN=3 (below 5) -> 44, LN=25 (above 20) -> 44, record unchanged. The 'changes made ... by the FORMAT clause' qualifier is vacuous here: the FORMAT clause is Annex A.4.8, declared Not claimed in docs/CONFORMANCE.md (named decline), so no record length is ever FORMAT-changed. cite.py --check 14.9.35.4 GR20 -> OK. No spec-derived REWRITE test pins the bounds. [editions as adjudicated: 2023; ISO 1989:2023 Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change to this rule (E.3.3 item 41 touches GR10 only), so 2014 identically; the 1985/2002 wording is not derivable from the 2023 text]
rows.rule-text: The number of bytes in the runtime representation of literal-1, the data item referenced by identifier-1, or the record referenced by record-name-1 after any changes made to the record length by the FORMAT clause shall not be larger than the largest or smaller than the smallest number of bytes allowed by the RECORD IS VARYING clause associated with file-name-1 or the file-name associated with record-name-1. If this rule is violated, the execution of the REWRITE statement is unsuccessful and the I-O status in the rewrite file connector is set to '44'.

rows.subject: REWRITE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: "For a file accessed in either random or dynamic access mode, the operating environment logically replaces the record identified by the relative key data item ... If the file does not contain the record specified by the key, the invalid key condition exists ... '23'." KeyedIoEmitter.EmitRewrite sets the relative key from the RELATIVE KEY item (FileSetRelativeKey) for non-sequential access; RelativeConnector.Rewrite (non-sequential) returns RecordNotFound '23' when the slot is absent, else Put at _pendingKey. Probe pd.cob (DYNAMIC): RK=7 absent -> 'IK7 ST=23', RK=1 -> 00 and a later READ of key 1 returns the new content. KeyedIoDifferentialTests.Relative_RandomRewriteDelete_StatusAndNotInvalidContract cites GR21 but is AssertSameAsLegacy - a regression net, not a spec-derived test - so test-ref empty. cite.py --check 14.9.35.4 GR21 -> OK. [editions as adjudicated: 2023; ISO 1989:2023 Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change to this rule (E.3.3 item 41 touches GR10 only), so 2014 identically; the 1985/2002 wording is not derivable from the 2023 text]
rows.rule-text: For a file accessed in either random or dynamic access mode, the operating environment logically replaces the record identified by the relative key data item specified for file-name-1 or the file-name associated with record-name-1. If the file does not contain the record specified by the key, the invalid key condition exists. When the invalid key condition is recognized, the execution of the REWRITE statement is unsuccessful and the I-O status in the rewrite file connector is set to the invalid key condition '23'.

rows.subject: REWRITE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: indexed ACCESS SEQUENTIAL - the prime key of the record to be replaced shall equal the prime key of the last record read, else unsuccessful with '21'. cite.py --check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 22). IndexedConnector.Rewrite (Access == Sequential) compares KeyOf(image, PrimeKey) with _lastReadPrime through KeyEq (collating-sequence equality) and returns SequenceError '21' with no update. Probe probe/rewrite-statement-p2/p1.cob: READ K001, MOVE "K002" TO key, REWRITE with INVALID KEY -> IK21 taken, NIK21 not, KEYCHG=21, record area unaffected (K002A01V01), K002 not overwritten (READ2 = K002A02V02). The collation-equal half is pinned by conformance:2002/ca17_indexed_rewrite_collating (FS=00 under ALPHABET A ALSO a), but no spec-derived golden pins the '21' outcome itself (KeyedIoDifferentialTests are legacy differential, disqualified) -> test-needed for the '21' arm. [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023]
rows.rule-text: If the access mode of the REWRITE file connector is sequential, the record to be replaced is specified by the value of the prime record key. When the REWRITE statement is executed the value of the prime record key of the record to be replaced shall be equal to the value of the prime record key of the last record read using this file connector. If it is not, the execution of the REWRITE statement is unsuccessful and the I-O status in the rewrite file connector is set to the invalid key condition, '21'.

rows.subject: REWRITE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: indexed random/dynamic - the record replaced is the one with the prime key; none -> unsuccessful, '23'. cite.py --check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 23). Rewrite looks up target by KeyEq on the prime key and returns RecordNotFound '23' before any mutation. Probe probe/rewrite-statement-p2/p1.cob (ACCESS DYNAMIC): absent K009 -> IK23 taken, ABSENT=23; after READ K001, REWRITE of K002's image -> DYNOTHER=00 and K002 now K002A02NEW (replacement by prime key, not by last read); REWRITE without any preceding READ -> DYNNOREAD=00 (no GR5 gate outside sequential access). Only KeyedIoDifferentialTests.Indexed_RandomCrudByPrimeKey covers it, and it is a legacy differential (AssertSameAsLegacy) -> does not close; test-needed. [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023]
rows.rule-text: If the access mode of the rewrite file connector is random or dynamic, the record to be replaced is specified by the prime record key. If there is no existing record in the physical file with that prime record key, the execution of the REWRITE statement is unsuccessful and the I-O status in the rewrite file connector is set to the invalid key condition, '23'.

rows.subject: Relational operators
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'Format 1 specifies simple relational operators.' (cite.py --check 8.7.5.2 -> OK 1)). Definitional; its only observable consequence is §8.8.4.12.2's choice among NOT / simple-relational-operator / extended-relational-operator after a logical operator. All six Format-1 spellings (GREATER THAN, >, LESS THAN, <, EQUAL TO, =) parse as one operator and evaluate correctly, and in abbreviated position ('A > B AND ... ') they are carried as simple operators (probe/relop/relpos.cob (A=5 vs B=3 and B=5, IF with every printed spelling, --std 2023 and 85); relabb.cob X4 'A <> B AND C' = T). No simple spelling is misclassified. No dedicated spec-derived test. [editions as adjudicated: 2023 (clause text, no edition qualifier); 2014 identical (Annex E, the 2014->2023 delta, lists no change); 1985/2002 text not in-repo, so the edition at which <> (and >=/<=) entered is NOT derivable here - the compiler accepts every spelling at every --std]

rows.subject: Relational operators
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: '> is an abbreviation for GREATER THAN.' (cite.py --check 8.7.5.2 -> OK §8.7.5.2 3)). The grammar admits '>' (comparisonOperator alt) and MapOperator normalizes the concatenated token text (IS/THAN/TO stripped, NOT inverts) so '>' and 'GREATER THAN' map to the same C# operator; the >>IF evaluator's private copy is textually identical. Probe probe/relop/relpos.cob (A=5 vs B=3 and B=5, IF with every printed spelling, --std 2023 and 85): the symbol and word forms give identical truth values at both data points (AB TTTFFFFFF|TTTTTFFFFFTTT / AC FFFFFFTTT|TTTTTTTTTTFFF at both editions), all as derived from the rule. [editions as adjudicated: 2023 (clause text, no edition qualifier); 2014 identical (Annex E, the 2014->2023 delta, lists no change); 1985/2002 text not in-repo, so the edition at which <> (and >=/<=) entered is NOT derivable here - the compiler accepts every spelling at every --std]
rows.rule-text: > is an abbreviation for GREATER THAN.
